pages.text: "Today, I'll roll stones and throw shells!" Taro flipped a big leaf over. Stones and shells tumbled onto the ground beneath the porch. Tidying could wait; playing came first.
"I'll play here tomorrow, too!" Taro left everything and climbed onto the porch. His Mom, working there, glanced underneath. There was nowhere to put a foot.
Stepping under the porch, Taro cried, "Ouch!" and jumped. He had stepped on a sharp stone. "Why does it hurt down here?"
His tapping branch was missing, too. Not under the stones, not between the shells. "I lost my branch..." Tears filled his eyes.
Sharp-eared deer Mumu bounded over. "Why are you crying?" Mumu looked beneath the porch. "There are three coconut shells here!"
Mumu lined up the three halves. "Stones in this one, shells in that one, branches in the other." Mumu sang, "After Playing, Into the Shells!"
Taro's hands were eager to move. He rolled in stones and rattled in shells, singing along. "After Playing, Into the Shells!" Each container filled up.
When the last shell went in, the space was clear. There was the branch underneath! Taro picked it up and tapped twice: tok-tok, tok-tok. "Tidying made what I wanted turn up!"
Taro held up three fingers and chanted, "One, gather matching things! Two, into the shells! Three, a clear space under the porch!" The next evening, he put his play stones away first.

Mom lifted Taro into a hug. "There's room to step now!" After tidying, nothing hurt his feet, and missing things appeared. Taro rested a hand on Mumu's shoulder and smiled. "After Playing, Into the Shells!"
